subject: RFP: open-model derivative usage & version stewardship questionnaire
messages:
From: Julia Smith <j.smith@novus.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Novus Legal <legal@novus.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Mar 2028 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: RFP: open-model derivative usage & version stewardship questionnaire

Hi David,

Thanks for taking Novus's RFP. We're narrowing down vendors for model distribution and need a clear statement on three items for our procurement packet:

1) Derivative usage: can Novus redistribute model-derived outputs (including fine-tuned derivatives) to partners and customers under the open models you serve? Are there restrictions for commercial redistribution or required attribution?

2) Provenance & SBOM: do you provide an auditable provenance record / SBOM for models in your catalog (origin commit, license, training-data attestations)? How often are these records refreshed when a source model updates?

3) Version pinning & update notices: what is your default policy for pushing model updates to Hosted endpoints? How do customers pin versions and get notified of upstream model changes and security/behavioral regressions?

We attached the RFP excerpt (Novus_RFP_part3.pdf) and would like a written response we can include in our vendor scorecard by EOD Wednesday 2028-03-14. If you have a one-page policy or artifacts, attach them.

Best,
Julia Smith
Sr. Procurement Manager
Novus Therapeutics

--

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Julia Smith <j.smith@novus.ai>
Cc: Novus Legal <legal@novus.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: open-model derivative usage & version stewardship questionnaire

Julia —

Appreciate the clear questions. I've outlined concise answers below and attached our policy artifacts (redwood_derivative_policy.pdf) and a practical pinning playbook (pinning_playbook.xlsx). Short answers first, then a brief expansion.

1) Derivative usage
- Short answer: Customers may redistribute outputs and fine-tuned artifacts generated using models served via Redwood, subject to the source model's license. For models under permissive OSS licenses (e.g., Apache-2.0, MIT), redistribution is permitted. For models with more restrictive terms (e.g., certain copyleft or custom licenses), we surface those constraints in the catalog and include recommended redline language.

2) Provenance & SBOM
- Short answer: Yes — we publish provenance metadata for each catalog entry: source repo/commit, license text, model weights checksum, known training-data attestations, and ingestion timestamp. Provenance is included in the model detail page and downloadable as a machine-readable SBOM (JSON). We refresh provenance when a new upstream release is onboarded or when our supply-chain monitors detect a material attribution change.

3) Version pinning & update notices
- Short answer: By default Hosted endpoints are pinned to a model artifact version; automatic updates do not happen unless a customer enables a managed "auto-roll" option. We provide deprecation notices 90 days before we remove or change a pinned version's compatibility (and a 30-day security hotfix channel where applicable). Customers can pin by model-artifact-id and request a compatibility snapshot from us.

Details and practical notes:
- Catalog UI/API: the model object includes model_id, artifact_id, license_id, origin_commit, checksum, and last_validated timestamp. These are exported as an SBOM (attached).
- Commercial repackaging: for certain third-party models where upstream licenses prohibit redistribution, we offer a managed-hosting-only option and provide recommended contract language; this is noted in the model metadata.
- Attributions & Notices: we provide both human-readable attribution language and machine-readable attribution tags that can be embedded in license manifests.
- Change governance: we maintain an internal Change Log and a customer-facing bulletin for catalog changes. Critical security/emergent behavior regressions trigger immediate notices and a suggested mitigation path; otherwise, we follow the 90-day deprecation cadence above.

I've attached the two artifacts requested. If Novus Legal wants specific redline language for your master services agreement (MSA), send over the clause and we can propose wording. Happy to hop on a 20–30m call if that helps.

Thanks,
David Kim
Head of Solutions — RedTeam (Redwood Inference)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Mar 2028 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Novus RFP draft wording + two small asks

David / Neha —

Thanks for the quick turnaround to Novus. Reviewed David's reply and attachments — looks solid. A couple of suggested clarifications before we send a slightly edited public copy back to Julia that should tighten up procurement review:

1) Commercial redistribution language: add a short sentence that we will surface "repackaging exceptions" per-model in the catalog and that for downstream commercial redistribution we can provide a single-line indemnity appendix (subject to legal review). This helps procurement score vendor risk.

2) Update/deprecation cadence: change the phrasing from "90 days" to "90-day deprecation notice, except for security hotfixes which are immediate with 30-day compatibility support". That balances customer expectations.

3) Evidence artifacts: call out that provenance SBOM exports include a signed (timestamped) checksum and a verification header that can be used in customer audits; include a note about SOC 2 evidence being available for customer review under NDA.

4) DocuSign / next steps: propose we attach a one-page addendum (DocuSign link) that contains the redline clause options (managed-hosting-only vs repackaging + indemnity). If Novus signs, we fast-track procurement.

If that sounds good I'll prepare a concise reply (one page) and include the two attachments David already provided plus the addendum link.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

David / Marissa,

Thanks for the rapid and thorough response. Novus Legal reviewed the materials and we have two minor requests before we score you as "acceptable" in our vendor packet:

1) Can you add the explicit phrase in the policy PDF: "Redistribution of model-derived artifacts is allowed when the upstream model license permits commercial redistribution; otherwise redistributions require prior written consent from Redwood and the upstream rights holder." That exact sentence is easier for our panel to score.

2) We accept the 90-day deprecation plus 30-day security window, but ask that the SBOM export include the timestamped checksum verification header you mentioned so auditors can validate the artifact without additional vendor interaction.

If you can confirm those two items and post the updated policy PDF to the HubSpot link (or send back via DocuSign for signature), we will move forward to commercial (PO) review next week.

Appreciate it —
Julia Smith
